headline: Nussmeier, Cake Strike With 10 Seconds Left to Steal 27-24 Win
dek: LSU improves to 2-0 and drops to fourth in the power poll while Arizona State falls to 0-2 in the Western Pacific.
body: Fourth and goal at the Arizona State 17, ten seconds on the clock, LSU trailing 24-20 — Garrett Nussmeier stood tall in a collapsing pocket and found Scott Cake streaking across the back of the end zone for a 17-yard touchdown that flipped the score to 27-24. Lilian Munoz drilled the extra point as time expired, and the Tigers walked off the field with a victory that felt impossible thirty seconds earlier.

Arizona State struck first blood on a 16-yard strike from Brock Thomas to Gary Bryant for a 7-3 lead late in the opening quarter, but a Jakailin Johnson interception returned 34 yards to the one-yard line set up Nussmeier's two-yard dart to Webb Jax that put LSU up 10-7 at the half. The Sun Devils answered with a field goal to tie it, then a 21-yard Munoz boot nudged the Tigers ahead 13-10. Thomas hit Tez Johnson from 11 yards to make it 17-13 early in the fourth, Nussmeier countered with a 20-yard laser to Cake for a 20-17 edge, and Thomas found Johnson again from five yards with 1:09 remaining to push Arizona State in front 24-20 — setting the stage for the final 53-second, 65-yard march.

The box score tells a story of Arizona State controlling the ball — 355 yards to 250, 21 first downs to 18, a 61 percent third-down clip against 23 percent — yet the Sun Devils coughed up the only turnover, a Thomas pick that handed LSU a first-and-goal at the one. Nussmeier made the most of his 212 yards and three scores, pushing his season line to 416 yards, five touchdowns and zero interceptions, while Cake's 117-yard, two-touchdown night vaulted him to third in the league with 172 receiving yards. Arizona State's defense notched three sacks from Mothudi, but the Tigers converted both fourth-down tries and committed only three penalties for 20 yards, the cleaner operation when the margin vanished.

LSU moves to 2-0 atop the Eastern Southern despite slipping from first to fourth in the power poll, averaging 32.5 points while the defense yields 388 yards a game — ninth in the league. Arizona State drops to 0-2 and fourth in the Western Pacific, the power poll tumbling from tenth to fourteenth, with the offense averaging 343.5 yards but the defense allowing 376. Next week the Tigers travel to Michigan (1-1), while the Sun Devils host unbeaten Washington.
turningPoint: Fourth and goal at the Arizona State 17 with ten seconds left in the fourth quarter, Nussmeier hit Cake for a 17-yard touchdown to make it 27-24.
byTheNumbers: Arizona State dominated time of possession 31:09 to 28:51 and converted 11 of 18 third downs, yet the lone turnover — a Thomas interception returned 34 yards — directly produced LSU's first touchdown.
LSU gained only 250 total yards, 17th of 18 teams this week, but Nussmeier's 212 passing yards and three touchdowns yielded a ruthless efficiency.
Cake's 117 receiving yards on seven catches accounted for the bulk of LSU's passing production and lifted his season total to 172 yards, third in the PCFL.
Both teams were perfect on fourth down (2-for-2 and 1-for-1), but LSU's two conversions included the game-winning drive while Arizona State's lone try came on a successful fourth-down attempt.

unsungHero.name: Jakailin Johnson
unsungHero.why: His 34-yard interception return in the second quarter gave LSU first-and-goal at the one, setting up the touchdown that erased Arizona State's early lead and shifted momentum before halftime.
